 -3-  MFA No. 1815 of 2021  JUDGMENT 1.

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 16.07.2018 passed in MVC.No.3130/2016 by IX Additional Small Causes Judge & XXXIV ACMM, Court of Small Causes, Member, MACT-7,
Bengaluru (for short the 'Tribunal') the present appeal is filed by the petitioners therein for Smt Thulasamma vs K P Natarajan on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90963555/
2 enhancement of compensation awarded.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, on 11.03.2016 at about 9.15 p.m., the deceased Venkataraju was standing in front of Jain Temple situated in Bengaluru - Hosur Road N.H.7 Road, Anekal Taluk,
at that time, the driver of KPN travels bus bearing registration No.PY-01-CF-9919 being driven in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against the deceased Venkataraju, because of which he died.
Petitioners are dependants of deceased Venkataraju.

4. Based on the pleadings and the evidence let in, the Tribunal concluded that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the bus and awarded compensation of Rs.14,87,416/-
to the petitioners.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners have preferred this appeal.
5. Admittedly, the accident is of the year 2016.
The petitioners have not established the income of the deceased.
Hence, the same has to be fixed as per chart of lok-adalath notionally at Rs.9,500/-.
The deceased was aged about 43 years at the time of the accident.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121], a multiplier of '14' has to be adopted.

entities.text: Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the law down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680, 25% needs to be added to his income.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Given the number of dependants, 1/4th of income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.

Thus, on the count of loss of dependency, petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.14.96,250/- (9,500 + 25% x 12 x 14 x 3/4).
6.

Further, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644], there are five dependants and they are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium(Rs.40,000x5= 2,00,000).

entities.text:
New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Thus, in all, they are entitled to a sum of Rs.17,26,250/- as against Rs.14,87,416/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Given the bank rate of interest, 6% p.a. is awarded for the enhanced compensation.

7. Hence, the following:-
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and enhanced to Rs.17,26,250/- as against Rs.14,87,416/- awarded by the Tribunal.
